newsitem.title: JORDAN: U.S. Navy and Jordanian army begin exercise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Navy and Jordanian army begin exercise.

text.p: U.S. and Jordanian troops have begun joint military exercises to improve coordination between U.S. Navy amphibious forces and Jordan's army, the United States embassy said on Thursday.
It said sailors and marines of the U.S. Fifth Fleet arrived in Jordan on Monday to take part in the arms training exercise known as "Infinite Moonlight 97". The exercise is set to run until June 19.

Jordan, a key U.S. ally in the Middle East since it signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994 and turned its back on neighbouring Iraq, has held regular joint exercises with U.S. forces and received substantial military aid from Washington.

In December it took delivery of $100 million worth of used tanks, trucks, navy vessels and helicopters. By early next year it is also due to receive a squadron of F-16 fighter bombers worth $200 million.
